answer: Each identity stores one marble slab in its forge vault and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a slab record, and a prism scanner reads the slab code. An auditor recomputes the record from the forge inventory log and the slab registry; a missing slab, reused code, or code that does not match the registry burns the bond. A fake needs a new slab: first 34, k-th 34+5(k-1), 1000th 5029, so 1000 fakes pay 2,531,500 with 70,000 at risk. A rented-slab ring fails: one slab cannot be in two forge vaults without duplicate codes in the registry. An honest slab pays 34 once and keeps its bond.
